title: "Log it"
prompt: The agent's next move — pick one, then see where it leads:

setup.text: Good session. Log it before we wrap.
Three hours of migration work, two decisions, one dead end. The log entry I write now is what future-you gets instead of remembering any of it.

options.label: [appends] "### 16:40 — migr sesh: idx rebuild via B-plan (post-bikeshed), perf ✓ after JSONB pivot, punted on the FK cascade q, see thread. TODO: vac-full before cutover."

outcome.text: Three weeks later: what was "B-plan"? What bikeshed? Which thread?

No idea — that session's context is gone, and the entry was written in its private shorthand. "See thread" points at a conversation that no longer exists. The log recorded that things happened without recording what they were.

options.verdict: Logged in the working register: session jargon, dangling references, compression that only decompressed inside a context that's now gone. The reader is future-you, cold — and future-you just got nothing.

options.label: [appends] "### 16:40 — Migration session. Rebuilt the search index with the JSONB approach — chose it over the join-table because query time dropped 40ms in the probe. Deferred the foreign-key cascade question; open because delete semantics aren't decided. Next: run vacuum before cutover."

outcome.text: Three weeks later, new session: "where did we leave the migration?"

Reading the log: JSONB approach chosen for the 40ms probe win, cascade question still open pending delete semantics, vacuum still owed before cutover. I'm oriented — picking up from the cascade decision. Total catch-up cost: one file read.

options.verdict: Plain sentences, decisions with their why, open threads named: the entry paid out exactly when designed to — a cold session (agent or human) orients in seconds from what would otherwise be archaeology.

options.label: The log's been getting messy — I'll take this chance to rewrite today's whole file as one polished narrative, folding the morning's rough entries into a clean summary of the day.

outcome.text: The morning entry said the JSONB idea came from the perf probe — I wanted to check the number. Where'd it go?

Smoothed away in the rewrite. The polished narrative reads better and remembers less — I edited a record as if it were a draft, and the rough details that made it a record were exactly what got polished out.

options.verdict: The log is append-only because it's a record, not a document: rewriting for polish destroyed the raw detail that gave it evidentiary value. Yesterday's entry is evidence — never a draft.
